Al Jazeera, News, Cybersecurity. LD datePublished Thu 15 Oct 05:15 BST; dateModified 05:18 BST. By Al Jazeera Staff.
Headline: 'X suspends 13,000 accounts, alleging foreign influence ahead of US midterms'.
X has suspended more than 13,000 accounts related to three suspected foreign influence operations linked to IRAN, RUSSIA AND CHINA that sought to shape US political debate. Announced Wednesday as X outlined measures ahead of the 3 NOVEMBER US midterm elections.
X said investigations found the networks used fake accounts to post and amplify political content targeting candidates and public figures 'across the political spectrum'. Accounts identified through 'proactive sweeps and investigations' under rules against spam and coordinated inauthentic behaviour.
X Global Government Affairs: 'Free speech is the bedrock of a functioning democracy, and we are proud that X is the global town square where these debates happen. Our job is to keep that conversation authentic, open, and safe.'
X also outlined rules against misleading information on how, when or where to vote, attempts to suppress turnout, and voter intimidation including calls for violence near polling stations. Users can report election posts via a 'civic integrity' option to request a community note; X may apply labels to violating posts.
CONTEXT: comes a week after OpenAI said it had shut down two alleged influence operations from Russia and Iran that used ChatGPT to push fake journalist personas and run a 'think-tank' covertly spreading anti-Ukraine propaganda. In 2021, Twitter said it had suspended 238 accounts purportedly operating from Iran.
SINGLE-SOURCED on an approved outlet - Al Jazeera only. The underlying claim is X's own announcement, so the company is the primary source; no independent verification of the account numbers.
